Definition: a girdle; specifically the ephod or highpriest's shoulder-piece; also generally, an image
BiblicalUsage: Ephowd is the ephod, the priestly garment of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, with shoulder pieces and a breastplate of judgment. Samuel ministered before the Lord as a child, girded with a linen ephod; Gideon made an ephod of gold that became a snare; and Hosea says Israel shall abide many days without ephod or teraphim.
TheologicalSignificance: A holy thing can be worn rightly or wrongly, and the garment was never the problem — the heart was. I hold that the ephod proves it: on Aaron it pointed to God, and in Gideon's house it became an idol.
